title: From Discovery to Defence: How a CVE Enters the World
description: The lifecycle of a publicly disclosed vulnerability — from the moment it is discovered to the moment it is patched in production systems. Understanding this timeline explains why some CVEs have public exploits, why CVSS Temporal scores change over time, and why patch timing determines exposure window.

nodes.label:
Discovery
Researcher or Attacker
Finds the Weakness
nodes.detail: A security researcher, or sometimes an attacker, identifies a way to exploit a software weakness

nodes.label:
Responsible
Disclosure
Vendor Notified
nodes.detail: The researcher reports the issue privately to the vendor. Responsible disclosure gives the vendor time to patch before public release.

nodes.label:
CVE ID
Assigned
CVE-YEAR-NUMBER
nodes.detail: A CNA (CVE Numbering Authority) assigns a CVE identifier. This may happen before or after patching.

nodes.label:
Vendor Develops
Patch or Fix
nodes.detail: The vendor confirms the issue and develops a security patch or configuration-based mitigation

nodes.label:
Vendor Advisory
Published
nodes.detail: The vendor publishes a security advisory describing the vulnerability, affected versions, and the fix. This is often the first public disclosure.

nodes.label:
NVD Entry
Published
nvd.nist.gov
nodes.detail: The National Vulnerability Database publishes the full CVE entry with CVSS score, CPE, CWE classification, and references

nodes.label:
Public Exploit
Published
(Exploit-DB / GitHub)
nodes.detail: For some CVEs, working exploit code is published publicly — often within days of disclosure. This dramatically increases real-world risk.

nodes.label:
Administrators
Apply Patch
nodes.detail: System administrators patch their installations. The time between advisory publication and patch application is the exposure window.

caption:
The time between 'Vendor Advisory Published' and 'Administrators Apply Patch' is the exposure window — the period during which a system is publicly known to be vulnerable but not yet fixed.

For CVE-2021-41773 (Apache httpd 2.4.49), working exploits appeared within 24 hours of disclosure. The exposure window for unpatched servers was measured in hours.

CVSS Temporal score tracks where a CVE is in this lifecycle: does a proof-of-concept exist? Is the exploit functional? Is a patch available? As these factors change, the Temporal score adjusts — even when the Base Score stays fixed.
